{"type":"text","timestamp":1793304558467,"sessionID":"ses_e76b895cbffejfQ9g0goJrLuNe","part":{"id":"prt_18947fb2f001oTAa09Ehy5LN57","sessionID":"ses_e76b895cbffejfQ9g0goJrLuNe","messageID":"msg_18947e294001g7hMHiRahazMYJ","type":"text","text":"I wrote `primers.fasta` with one primer pair. The output plasmid is the input plus a 39-nt insertion (`tagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaa`) right after the `catatg` start site, before `gcaagggcg…`. Nothing else differs. One pair is enough because the forward primer carries the whole insertion as a 5' tail.\n\n```\n>fwd\ntagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaagcaagggcgaggagctgtt\n>rev\nctcatatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttcta\n```\n\n- **Forward primer:** 57 nt. The 39-nt insertion is a non-annealing 5' tail, followed by 18 nt that anneal to the template. The annealing part has a Tm of 63.81 °C by `oligotm`.\n- **Reverse primer:** 45 nt, entirely annealing, with a Tm of 63.81 °C by `oligotm`. It is the reverse complement of the 45 nt just upstream of the insertion site.\n- **Pair design:** the two primers sit back-to-back, with their 5' ends adjacent at the insertion site and no overlap. That is the design the Q5 site-directed mutagenesis kit expects. The kit's KLD step then re-circularizes the linear PCR product.\n- **Rules:** both annealing lengths are within 15–45 nt, both Tms are within 58–72 °C, and the pair differs by about 0.003 °C. Tm was computed with `oligotm` and your flags, on the annealing portion only.","time":{"start":1793304558466,"end":1793304558466}}}
